doc.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026

title: What the subway years taught her, including racism
summary: She says playing in the train stations taught her resourcefulness and showed her racism at street festivals, which prepared her for the work.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: the love of my life. You know? So you have to understand the sequence. So here I was without the blues and then look what happened because of that experience, because of taking care of the old man, building a business, getting him to be financially independent from the blues. I was able to have what I needed to relate, and also having been a musician for the year. You know I worked in the train stations where when it was sweltering, you know, the old man used to keep a bag of ice under his little bowler hat. You know I mean in the winter we would get frostbite, you know I couldn’t even hold the harmonica many times when it was cold in the train station. And we had the experience of incredible racism. When we were asked to do the street festivals they’d hire a better known band, and we’re not even talking a famous band but they’d have an all-white band and they’d have a stage for them and they’d make the blues band, you know me, the old man or a Japanese guitarist and this great drummer used to play for Jimi Hendrix at Small’s Paradise. They would make us play on the pavement in the street without shade over our head for three hours for a hundred bucks for the whole band. You know? When it would rain we couldn’t go under the protection of the stage. So there were a lot of things I gleaned from that experience. And I also knew what it was like to have part times getting by and being very proud and never asking for help because as a single parent in New York City forget it. You know you become very resourceful. So it really gave me I think more than an MBA, it gave me a lot of experience and knowledge that I never could have gotten another way – to help people who were in the same situation.
